claims.claim: The channeling of natural forces into the human world has shattered the purposefulness of the world.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The channeling of natural forces into the human world has shattered the very purposefulness of the world, the fact that objects are the ends for which tools and implements are designed.

claims.claim: In automation, the distinction between operation and product, along with the product's precedence over operation, has become obsolete.
claims.supporting_excerpt: In the mode of production ushered in by automation, the distinction between operation and product, as well as the product’s precedence over the operation (which is only the means to produce the end), no longer make sense and have become obsolete.

definitions.definition: Things that are not made but grow by themselves into whatever they become, originating from the Latin nasci or the Greek physis.
Courses of movement which are self-moving and therefore outside the range of wilful and purposeful interference.

distinctions.distinction: A natural thing's existence is not separate but is identical with the process through which it comes into being, whereas the products of human hands must be realized step by step and their fabrication process is entirely distinct from the existence of the fabricated thing itself.

output.segment_function: The author analyzes automation as the culminating point of modern technology, explaining how the introduction of natural and cosmic processes into the human world shatters the purposefulness of the human artifice, overturns the categories of homo faber, and shifts the fundamental question of technology from human comfort to whether machines and automatic processes now rule over the human world.
unresolved_context: The potential of future technology to channel universal forces of the cosmos around us into the nature of the earth.
